title: Classify two-block decoder signatures and count all six-port patterns
body:
## Result

This answers [#6691, open question 1](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6691). For any two positive port-block sizes, the **generic support census equals the entire rational census** of input-column and inverse-row block masks. The proof gives a signed integer witness for every realizable rational signature, a construction over every field with more than two elements, and necessary and sufficient binary exceptions.

| Two blocks of three ports | Profiles up to relabeling | Labeled signatures |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Generic, rational, or a field with more than two elements | 188 | **33,727** |
| Two-element field | 167 | **30,547** |

A simultaneous pivot chart reduces the problem to two off-diagonal rectangles. Three binary obstruction classes account for 3,150, 15 and 15 missing labels. The counting formula uses O(pq) arithmetic operations. For balanced blocks, the fraction of ordinary signatures missing over the binary field decays as d^(3/2) (16/49)^d / (4√π). [Proof](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9417d35f070e2a64b6b174d549013cdcc5233794/research/two-block-signatures/PROOF.md) · [Exact counting formula](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9417d35f070e2a64b6b174d549013cdcc5233794/research/two-block-signatures/COUNTING.md)

**Price consequence.** When enlarging either support cannot lower its message price, assigning each message to one block already attains the exact minimum. This holds even for label-dependent prices. A positive nonmonotone example instead costs 10 over the rationals and 11 over the two-element field. Exact separating prices and convex mixtures classify all 21 missing six-port profiles. These are stipulated tariffs. The result covers square bases and does not supply physical decoder prices or a new κ. [Worked matrix and prices](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9417d35f070e2a64b6b174d549013cdcc5233794/research/two-block-signatures/PROOF.md#5-exact-prices-under-monotone-support-tariffs)

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-block-signatures
```

- Constructed and literally inverted every labeled six-port witness over Q, F3 and F2 where applicable. All 188 profile records include an explicit rational matrix, a binary matrix when possible, and exact finite-field multiplicities. [Certificates](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9417d35f070e2a64b6b174d549013cdcc5233794/research/two-block-signatures/SIX-PORTS.json)
- An independent determinant/cofactor matching screen covered all 262,144 supports of a fixed six-port chart and all its message relabelings. It also recovered the prior 439 codes from all 65,536 four-port supports.
- The binary census compared all 714,240 complementary pairs. The ternary point-incidence census accounted for all 666,860,040 pairs by weighting 31 coordinate-symmetry orbits of the first subspace. Neither finite-field oracle imports the classification or witness constructor.
- Complete normal and optimized receipts agree. Twenty different private-copy faults were rejected in both modes. The official source-history check and export passed in a separate full-history checkout. The read-only export, SHA-256 `5075e5d5e7d0d945c973a3ddb45a2c8da987c4134b0585db6a74b91203d6a15a`, reran all six commands without changing any file. [Validation](https://github.com/SHIN09-git/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9417d35f070e2a64b6b174d549013cdcc5233794/research/two-block-signatures/VALIDATION.md)

## Science boundary and credit

Gonzalo Mier supplied the prior zero-one rational and generic four-port screens. Nick Petalas supplied the four-port complementary-space characterization and six-port handoff. The prior matched-plane COPY result also covers overcomplete factorizations. Determinant matchings, finite Grassmannian counts and row-space incidence are classical. Three-block signatures, fine port-by-port joint patterns and physical caller admission are separate questions. The independent algorithms share one assisted author. Prepared for SHIN09-git with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, testing and writing. Apache-2.0.
